question: Is there a genuinely new Mid-Atlantic Ridge hydrothermal field, independently confirmed after 2020-03-25, inside the approximate 20N-to-10S 2011-2015 hydrophone domain, whose location was not publicly knowable at the InterRidge v3.4 cutoff?

screened_cases.evidence: Rosgeologia public announcement dated 2020-02-07 described Koralovoe and Molodezhnoe as newly discovered fields; first-stage search work occurred in December 2019. This predates the 2020-03-25 InterRidge v3.4 completion cutoff.
Same public pre-cutoff discovery evidence as Koralovoe.

Puy des Folles already appears in InterRidge v3.4 at 20.5083N, -45.6417 with inactive-vent references and pre-2020 history. The 2023 expedition established spectacular active high-temperature venting but did not create a new location unknown to the cutoff inventory.

search_observation: The first literature sweep after applying both domain and information-cutoff gates did not yield a clean post-2020 vent-location holdout inside the hydrophone network. This negative result is retained rather than relaxing the rules.

positive_side_result.reason: Although the new northern vent fields cannot validate the 2011-2015 hydroacoustic rate, MGDS provides exceptionally rich raw and processed AUV data for Puy des Folles, EMARK and Hydra: 400 kHz multibeam/backscatter, 1 m grids, 0.5 m chimney grids at Puy, CTD, sidescan, 1-6 kHz CHIRP, navigation and processing scripts.

next_search_strategy: Inspect expedition reports and vent inventories for 2021-2026 discoveries specifically between 20N and 10S, including fields initially reported as plume-only then visually confirmed later.
Separate truly new field locations from new measurements at old field coordinates.
If no clean post-2020 in-domain field exists, do not force this holdout; use an independent temporal earthquake/vent inventory split or a geography-separated holdout instead.
Recover 2022 Table S1 before any later-site segment scoring.
